title: The effect of classroom size and ceiling height on college students' learning performance using virtual reality technology

stimuli.description: Four virtual classroom settings: Small and High Room (SHR: 9.0m x 4.5m x 3.9m), Small and Low Room (SLR: 9.0m x 4.5m x 3.0m), Big and Low Room (BLR: 9.0m x 6.9m x 3.9m), Big and High Room (BHR: 9.0m x 6.9m x 4.8m). All furnished identically.
stimuli.source: Figure 1 and Experimental scene design section

tables.description: Experiment equipment used for VR, physiological signal monitoring (EEG, ECG), and environment monitoring.
Statistical table of the characteristics of the participants (gender, age, BMI).
Content of the three task tests: Stroop effect, Digital calculation, and Reading.
Seven-level scale used for subjective questionnaire (pleasure, relaxation, focus, fatigue).
Pearson correlation analysis between task test performance (Stroop, Digital calculation, Reading) and HRV-LF/HF.
Active point (Ep) frequency statistics for the 34 participants across different brain regions.
Pearson correlation analysis between task test performance (Stroop, Digital calculation, Reading) and EEG-ẞ rhythm.
Pearson correlation analysis between subjective evaluations (Pleasure, Relaxation, Focus, Fatigue) and task test performance (Stroop, Digital calculation, Reading).

limitations: Limited sample population, increasing risk of Type II error.
Subjective evaluations collected only after task completion, not before and after.
"Ceiling effect" on task scores due to many participants scoring near-perfect.
Other related variables (e.g., personnel deployment, teacher/student presence) not assessed.
Potential differences between virtual and real environments.
